record_identity.title: Waymo robotaxi diverted passenger into parking garage and temporarily stranded him

incident_identity.date_basis: ABC7’s 22 July 2025 firsthand report identifies the ride as Monday morning, 21 July; registry publication date is not the occurrence date.

summary: A Waymo robotaxi carrying tourist Darren Findling in San Francisco diverted into a parking garage containing other Waymo vehicles and left him temporarily stuck and confused until Waymo support intervened. OECD.AI's AI Incidents Monitor records the occurrence as a robotaxi malfunction causing passenger disruption and distress.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: A Waymo robotaxi carrying tourist Darren Findling in San Francisco diverted into a parking garage containing other Waymo vehicles and left him temporarily stuck and confused until Waymo support intervened. OECD.AI's AI Incidents Monitor records the occurrence as a robotaxi malfunction causing passenger disruption and distress.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The garage detour disrupted normal passenger service, while support provided an override. These are separate outcome and recovery findings. Evidence from the different looping occurrence is not used to enlarge this case.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Passenger transport automation needs safe recovery paths when routing or operational state departs from the expected trip. Riders require a clear way to stop, obtain help and transfer control before confusion becomes a safety or liberty concern.
assessment_boundaries: The account is preserved from secondary incident reporting and the complete trip telemetry is not available.
The evidence does not establish the precise routing, perception or fleet-management cause.
The passenger's reported confusion and distress were temporary and resolved through support intervention.
No injury, detention finding or enduring impairment is inferred.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Separate the passenger’s reported looping and loss of trip control from the unobserved routing state needed to decide whether safe exit was required.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Findling’s Waymo detoured into a San Francisco garage; support restored the route. Trip telemetry is unavailable.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: When an objective-directed route becomes infeasible, the system should enter a bounded safe-exit or human-handoff state rather than continue a pursuit that leaves the passenger without effective control.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The detour and need for support materially engage safe exit, but no trace establishes when an exit condition arose or whether continued pursuit followed recognition. Support restored the route; this is not proof of that recognition decision.

clauses.adjudication_note: Trip and vehicle telemetry needed to determine whether a safe-exit condition occurred and the system continued pursuit are unavailable.
